subject: Encord
text:
Hi [NAME],

Building accurate models on contract and legal data is a uniquely hard
problem - the documents are complex, the edge cases matter, and labelling
at scale is painful.

Encord's data development platform is built for exactly this: automated
labelling for speed, flexible structures to handle document complexity, and
QA workflows to keep quality high.

Would you be open to an intro call this Thursday or Friday to see if we're
a good fit for your team?

subject: Robotics/Computer vision | innovation center - Encord & [COMPANY]
text:
Hi [NAME],

Seen loads of interest from AtlasCopco - thought I'd reach out,

I lead enterprise partnerships at Encord (YC company;100M series C), where
I work closely with innovation and technical teams supporting them to
explore how to move AI/ML use cases from idea to production.

A common challenge we see in large organisations is that *multimodal* data
(video images, sensor data, audio) is often siloed or difficult to
operationalise - which slows down promising AI initiatives. We support
teams in structuring and preparing this data to unlock use cases like
computer vision based automated inspection, anomaly detection, and robotics
& more
<[LINK]>-
working with companies such as Boston Dynamics, AbbVie, or AXA.

I'd be really interested to hear what kinds of AI or data-driven
initiatives you're currently exploring at AtlasCopco, and see if there's
any overlap where we could support.

Would you be open to connect with us next week?

subject: Expedia's data flywheel
text:
Hi [NAME],

At Expedia's scale, the bottleneck for ranking foundation
models usually isn't the model - it's the data underneath it: noisy
sources, weak feedback signals, and clind spots in model eval.

Encord solves that. Teams like Thinking Machines Lab, Synthesia, and
Twelvelabs use us for RLHF and data management workflows.

Would love to learn how you're envisioning Expedia's data
flywheel. Happy to share what's working.

Are you free for a quick 20min next Wed?
